morphology.shape: Spherical, enveloped virion with icosahedral capsid

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human oral and, less commonly, genital mucosa; establishes lifelong latency in sensory (typically trigeminal) ganglia
habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen with recurrent reactivation from latency

identificationClues: Multinucleated giant cells with intranuclear (Cowdry type A) inclusions seen on Tzanck smear of vesicle scrapings
PCR of vesicle fluid or CSP is the preferred diagnostic method
Reactivates from latency in sensory ganglia during stress, illness, or UV exposure
Painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base

diseases: Genital herpes (increasingly also caused by HSV-1)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Direct contact with infected oral secretions or lesions; can also be transmitted via oral-genital contact
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Extremely common worldwide; most infections are acquired in childhood; leading cause of sporadic viral encephalitis in the United States
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: PCR of CSF is far more sensitive than viral culture for diagnosing HSV encephalitis and is now the diagnostic standard

examFacts.importantTest: PCR of vesicle fluid or CSF; Tzanck smear showing multinucleated giant cells
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Establishes lifelong latency in sensory ganglia with periodic reactivation, unlike most other viral infections
